newsitem.title: PERU: Peru siege has press "hostages" on nearby roof.
newsitem.headline: Peru siege has press "hostages" on nearby roof.

text.p: A group of nine journalists afraid to give up their front-row view of the siege of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima where Marxist rebels held about 360 on Friday have felt trapped on a nearby roof for three days.

"We can't leave this spot because the police wouldn't let us back in," local photographer Johnny Laurente shouted to Reuters from the two-story house roof, where he could snap shots of the inside of the residence.
"It's as if we are taken hostage," another colleague yelled, adding he had not been able to change his clothing.

The owners of the house allowed the journalists up to the roof in the first hours after Tuesday night's assault on the compound. But police later left the journalists stranded by cordoning off the area.
In the street below, journalists, who have flooded into Lima from around the world, had little to watch for most of Friday and took to interviewing each other in a host of languages.
But late on Friday, in a flurry of action, they swarmed around vehicles to block the exit temporarily from the area of a group of 38 hostages suddenly freed by the guerrillas.
Their trapped colleagues filmed from above.
